A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same work, with matching architecture, datasets and experiments despite the changed title and format. All 13 and 22 pages were inspected. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both refer to separate supplementary material that is not supplied.

before.justification: V1 reports original self- and cross-reenactment comparisons, component ablations and qualitative results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–8.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports expanded quantitative results in Tables 1–3, alongside qualitative comparisons and motion-basis analysis.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the triplane encoder, per-Gaussian feature-space deformation, frozen X-NeMo motion encoder, AdaLN/MLP decoding, synthetic-data pipeline and losses. V2 clarifies sampling and loss aggregation; replacing 'distillation' with 'guidance' does not establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use FFHQ and FEED for synthetic training, CelebV-Text for the real-data ablation, and VOODOO-XP for self- and cross-reenactment evaluation. The replacement example in Figure 6 remains within the existing portrait-animation coverage.

E2.justification: V1 Table 1 and v2 Tables 1–2 contain the same comparators: LivePortrait, HunyuanPortrait, X-NeMo, GAGAvatar, InvertAvatar, VOODOO-XP and Portrait4D-v2, including the same retrained GAGAvatar and Portrait4D-v2 variants.

E3.justification: V2 adds PSNR and silhouette IoU, extends memory comparisons, broadens ablation metrics and removes AED from the main self-reenactment comparison. The reported learning rate changes from 0.0001 to 5e-5. FPS reporting explicitly includes sequential processing, preprocessing and fitting, replacing fitting-excluded headline values; the corresponding full-pipeline speeds already appeared in v1's Table 1 caption. These are reported setting changes, not proof of reruns.

E4.justification: The same three component ablations remain, but v2 Table 3 adds reconstruction and geometry measurements to v1 Table 2's AED, memory and FPS analysis, exposing additional tradeoffs. The motion-basis similarity analysis is retained as v2 Figure 4, formerly Figure 5. No new robustness experiment is supplied.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present point estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds reconstruction, silhouette and resource results and removes the main self-reenactment AED entries. The proposed method's self-reenactment SSIM changes from 0.8294 to 0.835 and LPIPS from 0.1864 to 0.181; cross-reenactment ID changes from 0.75 to 0.76, EMO from 0.771 to 0.785 and AED from 0.745 to 0.731. Since the reported learning rate also changes, these are revised results rather than established same-setting gains. Figure 6 replaces its first qualitative example.

T1.justification: The Gaussian parameterization and Equations 1–3 retain the same mathematical content. Neither version supplies formal proofs or theorems. Removing the informal teacher-quality bound changes interpretation, not a mathematical result.

C1.justification: The central contributions and 107.31 FPS claim remain. However, v2 strengthens v1's claim of mitigating diffusion artifacts into an explicit introductory claim that the method is 'free of inconsistency or hallucination issues.' The new title emphasizes an already reported speed.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's teacher-quality bounds and inherited synthetic-data error limitation, describes identity drift as resolved, and substitutes an eyewear limitation involving thin structures, reflection and refraction. It adds an explanation of identity-score confounding and narrows the spatial-deformation drawback from 'all other metrics' to expression accuracy. These substantially revise the paper's qualifications and interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page address and specifies that Gaussian count stays fixed while rendering resolution increases. It clarifies loss aggregation and revises the stated learning rate. Conversely, it omits v1's restriction of MEt3R evaluation to neutral-expression, pose-changing sequences, leaving that selection detail unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 removes the single-/few-step diffusion discussion and its four cited works, v1 references 30, 64, 65 and 105. It also explicitly acknowledges that person-specific optimization approaches can meet the three animation goals, distinguishing its instant, generalizable encoding. The remaining research positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, introduces 'portrait animation trilemma' terminology, replaces distillation/PCA phrasing with diffusion guidance and blendshape bases, and revises selected explanatory and discussion paragraphs. The section sequence and most exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted from two columns to predominantly one column, with resized and relocated figures. The combined benchmark table becomes separate self- and cross-reenactment tables, the ablation table gains columns, and colored cells replace bold/underlined rankings. Figures 4–5 exchange numbers, Figure 6 replaces one row, and Figure 7 is respaced.

improvement.justification: The expanded metrics and ablations improve empirical characterization, and explicit end-to-end timing improves clarity. However, v2 removes inherited-error caveats and claims freedom from hallucinations without corresponding robustness evidence. Figure 2 also retains InvertAvatar's 24.30 FPS despite Tables 1–2 reporting 0.07 FPS under the stated timing convention. These benefits and losses in qualification and consistency prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
